observation: TDD red phase (39 tests) written before implementation. All tests pass on first green run. Red phase caught all edge cases (role filtering, crash-path cleanup, bridge failure fallback) before code review.

Architecture critique (8/10) caught 3 real issues before code: crash-path cleanup, bridge-failure logging, Zod version claim. All addressed in implementation. Critique eliminated 1 review cycle + fix cycle (~4h cost saved).
Architecture plan's reconciliation table resolved 8 spec-vs-reality items before code (tool count, dependencies, phase integration, base URL, port passing). Zero mid-stream surprises.

One code review cycle (Round 1 WITH blocking finding → fix → Round 2 DONE). Unwrapped close() call in unregister broke catch pattern. Critique warned about this but builder missed the exact call site. Fixed fast (2h) due to critique priming.

Test-to-code ratio 5:1 (1201:234). High but correct for thin transport adapters. Integration test suite (664 lines, 10 tests) validates HTTP contracts. Track ratio across workpackages — should stay high for adapters, low for domain code.

Two-lens review model (architect + reviewer) effective. Phase 2 caught structural (crash-path, error-handling). Phase 4 caught implementation (unwrapped close). Neither redundant. Confirms CC-009 + CC-003 pattern.

Timeline: 5 days (concept → retro). 9 commits (1 per phase + integration). Productive commits: 7 (concept, architecture, tests, implementation, review, fix, retro). CI/doc commits: 2 (critique, code-review). Productive ratio 78%.
